given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)

breaks.break: Code treats a loan due before today as not overdue, so it sends nothing.
Code treats a loan due exactly today as overdue (`<=`).
Code treats a returned loan as open.

given.why: B1 sends for loans due 03-16 on 03-17 and expects exactly 2 sent, so a missed overdue loan fails. B2's loan due today pins the boundary.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today

breaks.break: Code skips every loan that has any reminder, including one recorded on an earlier day.
Code ignores today's reminders and always sends.

given.why: No test seeds a reminder from a previous day, so code that blocks on any past reminder would pass every test.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member

breaks.break: Code never calls the API.
Code sends the wrong member, such as the loanId as memberId.
Code sends the wrong dueOn or loanId.

then.why: The fake records the full reminder, and the test asserts memberId, loanId and dueOn for both loans.

then.part: then records a reminder for today

breaks.break: Code records nothing.
Code records dueOn instead of today.
Code records the reminder against the wrong loan.

then.why: The test reads the reminders table and checks loan_id and sent_on (03-17, which differs from dueOn 03-16) and the row count.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today

breaks.break: Code sends again on a second run the same day.
Code treats a reminder from another day as today's and skips the loan.

given.why: The second run proves a same-day reminder blocks a send. Nothing proves that a reminder from a different day does not.

breaks.break: Code reminds about returned loans.

given.why: loan2 is overdue but returned, and the only send expected is for loan1.

breaks.break: Code reminds about a loan due today (`<=`).
Code reminds about a loan not yet due.

given.why: loan3 is due on 03-17, today, so it sits on the boundary, and toMatchObject on the array fixes the length at 1.

breaks.break: The API is called for a skipped loan.

then.why: The sent list must contain only loan1 after two runs, so an extra send for any skipped loan fails.

breaks.break: Code treats a refusal as accepted.

given.why: The fake refuses loan1, and the test checks that no reminder is recorded for it.

breaks.break: The client lets a connection failure throw instead of returning refused.

given.why: B5's test maps a failed connection to refused, so the service sees the same case as a refusal.

breaks.break: Code records the reminder even after a refusal.

then.why: The reminders table must hold only loan2's row.

breaks.break: Code logs a different event name.
Code logs at info instead of warn.
Code logs nothing.

then.why: The assertion matches both level warn and event reminder.failed.

breaks.break: Code logs the memberId, or no loanId, in the loanId field.

then.why: The log assertion uses objectContaining on level and event only and never reads fields.loanId.

breaks.break: Code logs a fixed string such as "refused" instead of the refusal's reason.

then.why: The test sets the reason "Notifications API answered 503" at line 102 but never asserts it appears in the log.

then.part: and carries on with the other loans

breaks.break: Code stops the run at the first refusal.

then.why: loan1, the earlier and refused loan, is followed by loan2, which must still be sent and recorded.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan

breaks.break: Code logs the finish before all loans are handled, so the counts are partial.

given.why: Three overdue loans (two accepted, one refused) are all handled, and the final counts must be 2 and 1.

breaks.break: Code uses a different event name.
Code logs at warn.
Code logs something after the finished entry.

then.why: logs.at(-1) must equal the exact info entry for reminders.finished.

breaks.break: Code never increments the sent count.
Code never increments the failed count.
Code swaps the two counts.

then.why: The fields are asserted exactly as sent 2 and failed 1, and the unequal values distinguish a swap.

breaks.break: The client needs extra input that a due reminder doesn't supply.

given.why: Every test calls the client with a full reminder of memberId, loanId and dueOn.

breaks.break: Code uses PUT or another method.
Code uses a different path, such as /notification.

then.why: The captured request must match method POST and path /notifications exactly.

then.part: with JSON `{ memberId, template: "loan-overdue", data: { loanId, dueOn } }`

breaks.break: Code sends a content type other than application/json.
Code renames memberId.
Code uses a different template name.
Code renames loanId or dueOn inside data.

then.why: toEqual on the whole body and the content-type header pins every key and value.

breaks.break: Code accepts only 200.
Code accepts only 200 and 202.

then.why: 200, 202 and 204 are all accepted, which rules out narrow status checks.

then.part: any other answer ... as refused, with a reason naming the status

breaks.break: Code refuses only 5xx.
The reason omits the status.

then.why: A 400 must give kind refused and a reason containing "400".

then.part: or a failed connection as refused, with a reason saying the API was unreachable

breaks.break: The client throws on a network error.
The reason doesn't say unreachable.

then.why: A connection error must give kind refused with a reason containing "unreachable".
